# testdata

Labelled, sanitised corpus of **100 samples (50 phishing / 50 legitimate)**. **Headers only** — bodies, attachments, links and personal data are stripped.

## Sources and licences
- **Phishing:** Nazario phishing corpus, phishing-2023 archive, https://monkey.org/~jose/phishing/ — CC-BY-4.0 (attribution required). Note: 2023+ archives are NOT anonymised; samples are stored headers-only.
- **Legitimate:** Apache SpamAssassin public corpus, `easy_ham`, `easy_ham_2` and `hard_ham`, https://spamassassin.apache.org/old/publiccorpus/ — public corpus.
- **Raw/unmodified originals:** kept out of git in `testdata/raw/` (git-ignored). The SpamAssassin `spam_2` archive was downloaded as spare material and is unused.

## Composition notes
- Legitimate set deliberately includes hard cases: mailing lists (`List-Id`), bulk mail (`Precedence: bulk`), newsletters (`List-Unsubscribe`), thread replies and forwarded messages. These are the false-positive canaries.
- Phishing set is dominated by brand impersonation (Netflix, PayPal, DHL, UPS, USPS, Apple, Amazon, banks); most samples pass or lack SPF/DKIM/DMARC, which is why authentication alone is not a sufficient signal.

## Layout
- `phishing/`, `legitimate/`: sanitised samples used by the engine and golden tests.
- `splits/`: reproducible 70/30 development/holdout split (`dev.txt`, `holdout.txt`) generated by `tools-python/split_corpus.py`. Tune against dev only; the holdout stays untouched until a phase ends.
- `malformed/`: deliberately broken files for parser robustness tests.
- `raw/`: git-ignored originals. Never commit anything from here.
- `labels.csv`: `file,label,source,confidence,notes` per sample.

## Regenerating
```
python tools-python/grow_corpus.py     # extend to the target size (deterministic)
python tools-python/rename_corpus.py   # descriptive domain-derived filenames
python tools-python/split_corpus.py    # rebuild the dev/holdout split
python -m pytest tools-python/tests -q # corpus invariants
```
